headline: Binance ties $6.43bn theft to a poisoned Homebrew install
standfirst: The largest single loss in this run is a developer-tooling story: a record-setting crypto theft traced to a tampered package install and a fake interview loop. Elsewhere, a 10.0-rated Siemens flaw is being used to backdoor industrial devices, a security vendor's own update channel was turned against its customers, and fixes land for Barracuda and Linux kernel issues.
bodyMarkdown:
## Breaches

Binance describes the $6.43 billion theft as the culmination of a "sophisticated, multi-stage campaign" rather than an isolated breach or simple phishing, and points to two entry lures: a tampered Homebrew installation and recruitment-themed social engineering aimed at two of its engineers [[s8]]. The excerpt stops short of describing what the modified package did once installed, how long the intrusion persisted, or how the funds were moved — those details were not supplied. Analysis: the notable signal is the target class. Developer tooling and hiring pretexts sit on the workstation where credentials, keys and build access concentrate, which is consistent with the exchange's own framing of a multi-stage campaign, though the supplied text does not establish the sequence beyond the two named lures.

Separately, the maker of cPGuard says an attacker broke into the product's update system and used it to push a malicious script to customers' Linux servers, installing a backdoor and collecting password hashes and other sensitive files — with some of that data since taken [[s14]]. The advisory excerpt begins listing a cPGuard version but is truncated, so the exact fixed-release guidance was not supplied. Analysis: an update channel is the highest-trust path into a security product's install base, and this is a live supply-chain compromise rather than a theoretical one.

## Actively exploited

A maximum-severity flaw in Siemens SIMATIC IoT2050 Advanced devices is under active exploitation according to VulnCheck, which reported attackers planting remote command backdoors [[s40]]. CVE-2026-58115 carries a CVSS 4.0 score of 10.0 and is a CWE-306 missing-authentication bug: the Node-RED HTTP interface does not enforce authentication, so an unauthenticated remote attacker can reach programming nodes capable of executing system commands and create malicious flows that run arbitrary code with maximum privileges. The affected configuration is devices running Industrial OS with Node-RED installed, versions earlier than V4.3.4.1. The CVE was not found in CISA's KEV catalog at enrichment; that is a confirmed catalog miss for this record, not evidence that exploitation has not occurred — and here the source reports exploitation directly.

Ransomware operators are encrypting Synology NAS devices by exploiting an already-patched DiskStation Manager vulnerability against systems running outdated DSM versions, with the vendor urging customers to update [[s38]]. No CVE identifier or exploitation mechanics were included in the supplied excerpt, so the specific flaw and the affected builds cannot be stated here.

## Vulnerabilities

Barracuda has disclosed two flaws that chain together: a pre-authentication authorization bypass and a command injection, together reaching root on a susceptible device [[s10]]. CVE-2026-116606 is the bypass, rated 9.3 under CVSS 4.0, and per NVD it affects Email Security Gateway versions earlier than 9.4.0.030, letting an unauthenticated remote attacker invoke a configuration-import function and restore a crafted, compatible backup archive — resulting in unauthorized modification of the appliance's global configuration. The command-injection half's CVE ID and score fall outside the truncated excerpt, so only the first is detailed here. Neither is in KEV, and no in-the-wild exploitation is reported. Analysis: the pre-auth bypass is the interesting half — it needs no credentials, but the described path is a crafted backup archive rather than a bare network probe.

Red Hat has shipped fixed kernels for a use-after-free in the Linux kernel's IPv4 TCP code, CVE-2026-98432, rated 9.8 under CVSS 3.1 and reachable by a remote, unauthenticated attacker [[s28]]. Kernels are available for the three most recent major Red Hat Enterprise Linux releases; Ubuntu's fixes for its three newest long-term-support releases remain in an opt-in testing channel with no date given for a regular update. Analysis: the asymmetry matters more than the score — one distribution's users can patch on a normal cadence while another's must opt in to testing to get the fix.

## Industry

Google has dismantled the XCPE botnet, which it says comprised 1.3 million Android devices and was created and operated for financial gain by Videostrong Technology, an Android OEM/ODM [[s34]]. Analysis: an operator that also manufactures the hardware sits upstream of any device-level control, which is the supply-chain risk the takedown illustrates; the supplied excerpt does not describe the botnet's capabilities or how devices were conscripted.

## Research

Google is warning that LLMjacking — hijacking enterprise access to large language models to burn expensive compute and AI services — is costing some enterprises up to $1 million in cloud charges [[s11]]. API keys are obtained through phishing, source code leaks, misconfigured environments or exposed client-side code. Analysis: the significant number is the bill, not the technique; resource hijacking that shows up first on a cloud invoice rather than in an EDR alert is easy to miss for exactly as long as it takes finance to notice.

nvd.description:
A vulnerability has been identified in SIMATIC IoT2050 Advanced (6ES7647-0BA00-1YA2) (All versions < V4.3.4.1 running Industrial OS with Node-RED installed). Affected devices do not enforce authentication on the Node-RED HTTP interface, allowing unauthenticated access to programming nodes that are capable of executing system commands on the server.
This could allow an unauthenticated remote attacker to create malicious flows through the HTTP interface in order to execute arbitrary code on the underlying server with maximum privileges.

selected.title: Red Hat Patches 9.8-Rated Linux TCP RCE Flaw While Ubuntu Releases Fixes for Testing
selected.excerpt: Fixed kernels for a use-after-free vulnerability in the Linux kernel's IPv4 TCP code are now available for Red Hat Enterprise Linux 8, 9, and 10, while Ubuntu's fixes for its three newest long-term-support releases remain in its opt-in testing channel with no date for a regular update. The flaw, tracked as CVE-2026-98432, can be reached by a remote, unauthenticated attacker and can

nvd.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

ipv4: free inet_opt and ireq_opt after an RCU grace period

tcp_v4_syn_recv_sock() transfers ownership of ireq->ireq_opt to the
child socket (newinet->inet_opt) without copying it.

Another cpu can concurrently process a retransmitted SYN for the same
request socket, and send a SYNACK from tcp_check_req().
tcp_v4_send_synack() and inet_csk_route_req() read ireq->ireq_opt
under rcu_read_lock() only, and ip_build_and_send_pkt() and
ip_options_build() then read opt->optlen twice.

Note that the SYNACK timer itself is not an issue: it holds a
reference on its request socket, and inet_csk_reqsk_queue_drop()
calls timer_delete_sync() before the child can be freed.

Since commit 079096f103fa ("tcp/dccp: install syn_recv requests
into ehash table"), request sockets are processed without holding
the listener lock, so nothing prevents the child socket from being
freed while the SYNACK is still being built. TCP child sockets do
not have SOCK_RCU_FREE, and inet_sock_destruct() frees inet_opt
with a plain kfree(), leading to a use-after-free in
ip_options_build().

A similar issue exists with request socket migration
(net.ipv4.tcp_migrate_req=1, or a BPF_SK_REUSEPORT_SELECT_OR_MIGRATE
program). reqsk_timer_handler() clones the request socket with
inet_reqsk_clone(), so that the old request socket and its clone
share the same ireq_opt, then reqsk_migrate_reset() clears the
pointer in the old one. Another cpu holding a reference on the old
request socket can still be using these options (sending a SYNACK,
or creating a child in tcp_v4_syn_recv_sock()) when the clone is
freed, and tcp_v4_reqsk_destructor() also uses a plain kfree().

Readers already use RCU, and other paths replacing inet_opt
(do_ip_setsockopt(), cipso_v4_sock_setattr()...) already use
kfree_rcu(). Use kfree_rcu() in inet_sock_destruct() and
tcp_v4_reqsk_destructor() as well.

IPv6 is not affected by the first issue, because tcp_v6_syn_recv_sock()
duplicates the options. tcp_v6_reqsk_destructor() has the same
migration issue with ipv6_opt, which is only set by CALIPSO. This
will be addressed in a separate patch.

selected.angle: Fixes are shipping for a 9.8-rated remote unauthenticated use-after-free in the Linux kernel's IPv4 TCP code (CVE-2026-98432), with Ubuntu still in opt-in testing.
